questions.prompt: Use your real or simulated trial. State your data source, horizontal distance, and total flight time. Then show your calculations for vx, vy, total initial velocity, and launch angle with units.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Grade the completeness and internal consistency of the student's own measurement and calculation chain. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2.
a. Full credit: Identifies the data source, gives distance and time in SI units, shows all four formulas and substitutions, and reports reasonable component speed, total speed, and angle values. Partial credit: Uses appropriate data and methods but has one missing calculation, unit, or arithmetic error. No credit: Provides no usable measurements or does not show a valid calculation chain.

questions.prompt: Write a conclusion defending your calculated launch velocity. Include the velocity in m/s and mph, explain how the horizontal and vertical components combine, and analyze at least two realistic measurement errors and how each could change the result.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: Grade the quantitative conclusion, vector reasoning, and directional analysis of measurement error. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3.
a. Full credit: Cites consistent m/s and mph results, explains vector-component combination, and analyzes two realistic errors with how each would raise, lower, or otherwise affect the calculated result. Partial credit: Gives a reasonable conclusion with incomplete component reasoning or only names errors without explaining their effects. No credit: Gives unsupported values or no meaningful analysis of the launch or its uncertainty.
